complete_examples.text: The Sato spectrum, which is widely used in wheel–rail rolling noise [31,32], wheel–rail wear [33], and high-frequency wheel–rail contact force [34], is used to generate short wavelength random track irregularities, in which the wavelength is below 1 m. The expression of the German low interference spectrum can be found in References [10,29], and that of the Sato spectrum can be found in Reference [29].
